correctness.rationale: Summing |a−b|=a+b−2min(a,b) over the simple cycle gives the deficit. Its zero event is independent support; counting a marked occupied vertex with positive cyclic gaps gives n/k times binom(n−k−1,k−1), and labelled surjections give k! S(N,k). In the common-sample coupling, U counts adjacent sample-index pairs. A mismatch T<U requires a specific doubled pair and a third observation at either cycle neighbor, with probability 2/n² per choice, and a union bound gives (N)_3/n². For a given pair, the dependency neighborhood contains itself and 2(N−2) other pairs; the latter each have joint success (2/n)^2 by conditioning on the common draw. All outside indicators collectively use disjoint draws, so b3=0. The local-dependence Chen–Stein bound in the sup-over-events convention is at most b1+b2; together the bound is N(N−1)(9N−16)/n². N=1 has zero deficit and mean; N=2 reduces to one adjacency indicator. This also holds for the triangle, where each vertex still has two distinct neighbors. The growing-mean Poisson normal limit is carried by TV under centering and scaling; the all-supercritical zero-event result follows by truncation at floor(n^(7/12)) and monotonicity, not by applying the bound outside its vanishing-error range.
residual_risks: Finite checks do not certify the limiting laws or Chen–Stein theorem. The TV error is not optimal. The sentence about orientation in Step 3 refers to either of the two cycle neighbors; the doubled sample pair is already fixed.

evidence: Standard local-dependence Chen–Stein controls the Bernoulli sum of sampled pairs U, including adjacency as the pair-success condition. The histogram T is not that sum: at counts 2 and 1 on adjacent bins their respective edge contributions are 2 and 1.
The cyclic moment paper keeps n fixed for its leading variance theorem; its traveling mode pertains to linear variance at n of order sqrt(N), not N of order sqrt(n).
broader_coverage.reasoning: The proxy bound is covered as a direct use of the general theorem. Transferring it to T needs control of triple occupancy and the exact numerator needs support counting. Neither fixed-bin moments nor the proxy theorem supplies those two steps.

checked_sources: Comb Test §II and Part 5 moment framework
value.rationale: The event of attaining maximal irregularity has a natural role in null calibration of an order-sensitive histogram statistic. The whole deficit law, explicit finite zero-event formula and change from a Poisson birthday law to Gaussian fluctuations give substantially more information than moments, and the closed coefficient can be used without simulating labelled samples. The novelty and value lie in the finite-to-sparse calibration, not in a new general approximation theorem.
residual_risks: No full-distribution assertion beyond the stated sparse range, no test-power claim, and no optimality claim for the error constant or window.
